rich_narrative.summary: The Against Malaria Foundation operates with a public score band of Below Average due to significant financial liquidity risks and limited alignment with specific Muslim donor priorities. In FY2025, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $119,395,632</cite> to fund long-lasting insecticidal nets in malaria-prone regions. Operational tracking indicates that <cite id="1">100.0% of public donations go directly to program expenses</cite>. The charity relies on detailed monitoring systems, including <cite id="4">smartphone surveys</cite> and <cite id="5">technical post-distribution reports</cite>, to evaluate whether nets remain hung and functional after distribution. However, serious financial vulnerabilities constrain its outlook. The charity holds <cite id="1">0.0 months of operating reserves</cite>, creating extreme continuity risk. Additionally, reported unit costs of $0.18 per beneficiary suggest that beneficiary counts may be inflated relative to total expenditure.
